doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Turning from playing to writing and Max Jones
summary: Realising the band would not succeed, he began writing reviews, helped by Melody Maker critic Max Jones.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You know we hadn’t improved like others of our equivalent had improved. And we realized that we were kind of playing catch-up. And I knew it wasn’t going to really happen. Jazz is a demanding music art form as we all know. And it was a bit late in the day.
Do you think that even that limited amount of playing you did in the genre helped you write?

What it made me want to do is to communicate. I mean the reason I write then and now is out of a desire to communicate about my enthusiasm for this music. It’s an evangelistic process as far as I’m concerned. I’m trying to stop people and trying to say hey, listen to this, experience it. And I think once I knew that we weren’t going to get very far by playing, a sort of odd sequence took place. I can just remember thinking I really ought to be writing about this, because it’s important and I want to make sure that other people get some sense of why it’s important. Now that’s all very pretentious but that is what was in my mind. So I started writing very early on in my twenties, once the bands started to kind of fall by the wayside, I started to have a go at trying to write reviews and just, well, see if I could get something into print.
Yeah. A lot of knocking on doors and trying to make connections?

Well a little bit of that. I was very much helped by a marvelous man called Max Jones who was the premiere jazz critic of the “Melody Maker.” I got to know him early and we stayed firm friends right through to the end of his life. And he let me put, he started to publish little bits by me in the “Melody Maker” in the late 50s, and that was helpful. By then I’d started corresponding with one or two musicians and things like that. And you could kind of pass on a few newsy tidbits, and they would go into Max’s column. So I got the taste for it that sort of way.
